html:
The Moose Cree are a Cree people of the Moose River basin and the west coast of James Bay, in northern Ontario. They speak a dialect of Cree and were first noted by the Jesuits in the 1670s.

They lived by hunting moose, caribou and geese, trapping and fishing, moving between winter hunting grounds inland and summer gatherings on the bay.

In 1673 the Hudson's Bay Company built a post at the mouth of the Moose River, later called Moose Factory. It is one of the oldest English settlements in Ontario, and the Moose Cree became central to the bay's fur trade as hunters, guides and provisioners. In 1905 they signed Treaty 9 with Canada. The Moose Cree First Nation is still based on Moose Factory Island. Neighbours: Abitibiwinni.
